introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Advanced Level Examination. Information and Communication Technologies (0796), Paper 3 (practical), June 2020. Duration: two hours. Answer ALL tasks.**

The booklet reproduced here contains two versions of the same practical paper, headed DAY 1 and DAY 2: they have the same two tasks (Task A: spreadsheet, 19 marks; Task B: database, 21 marks) with different file names, cell references and wording in a few questions.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. Do not write in pencil. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answer. Your results must be recorded in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Candidates must allow for themselves enough time to complete and check their work where these are required. The supervisor will guide you on how to save your files but usually you will be expected to save all your work in one folder named *Candidate folder* that will be created in your desktop. When an imperative programming language is required to write program code, either Standard [ISO] Pascal or [ANSI] C programming language may be used. You should ensure all your work is collected and printed before leaving the examination room. All printed work should be inserted in this booklet and well stapled. Carefully handle all equipment put at your disposal to avoid accidents that may lead to a disaster or system failure. Report any case of system or device malfunction to your supervisor.

The working files (the spreadsheet workbook and the database) are supplied on the day in the Candidate folder; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

Open the MDC workbook in the candidate folder. This workbook contains three worksheets: Sales, OldSales and Summary. *[Workbook supplied on the day, not reproduced here.]*

Questions 1 to 10 are based on the **Sales** sheet.

questions.enonce_markdown: Change the font type of the first row (showing SN, NAME, 5% Discount ...) to ALGERIAN. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the whole first row (click the row heading **1**, or select the header cells A1:G1), then on the **Home** tab open the *Font* box and choose **Algerian** (or Format Cells > Font > Font). Only the font *type* changes: the size, the text and the other cells stay as they are. If Algerian is not listed, it is not installed on that computer, and the supervisor is told.

*Marking:* 1 mark if every header cell of row 1 (SN, NAME, 5% Discount, ...) is in Algerian.

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert cell border in the range A1:G25. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the range **A1:G25** (click A1, then Shift + click G25; or type A1:G25 in the Name Box). On the **Home** tab open the *Borders* menu and choose **All Borders** (or Format Cells > Border > *Outline* and *Inside*, then OK). The outline AND the inner grid lines must both appear, so that every cell of the range has a border on its four sides.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the outside border, 1 mark for the inside borders.

questions.enonce_markdown: Adjust the Name field width to 138 pixels. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Right-click the heading of the Name column (column B) and choose **Column Width...** (or Home > Format > Column Width). In Excel with the default font (Calibri 11) one character is 7 pixels wide and each column adds 5 pixels of padding, so 138 pixels = 19 x 7 + 5 corresponds to a width of **19** characters: the dialog box then shows *19.00 (138 pixels)*. The same value appears in the pop-up when the column boundary is dragged with the mouse.

*Marking:* 1 mark for a Name column whose width is 138 pixels.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Insert a formula in the *5% Discount* field to calculate the discount for each item bought.

This discount is 5% of the product of Unit Price and Quantity. *[2 marks]*

Write down the formula in cell C2.

*(answer line: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The discount is 5% of (Unit Price x Quantity). In the sheet the 5% Discount field is column **C**, the Payable Total is column **F** (both are named in the question) and the numeric fields Unit Price and Quantity are in columns **D** and **E** (the printed paper does not show the sheet: this layout is deduced from the cell references of questions 4 to 6, from the range of question 9 and from the order requested in question 8). The formula is typed in the first data cell and copied down the column (fill handle), so the row number changes automatically:

```
C2: =0.05*D2*E2
```

Equivalent forms are accepted: `=5%*D2*E2`, `=D2*E2*0.05`, `=(D2*E2)*5/100`. The formula must start with `=`, use cell references (not typed numbers such as 495), and the multiplication sign `*` (not x). Check: for a unit price of 900 and a quantity of 11, the product is 9,900 and the discount is 9,900 x 0.05 = 495.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the 5% factor, 1 mark for the product of Unit Price and Quantity with correct references.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Insert a formula in the *Payable Total* field to calculate the total price for each sale. The total is calculated following the algorithm below

```
Start
    Multiply Unit Price by Quantity to get total price
    Subtract the 5% Discount from the total price above
Stop.
```

Write down the formula to calculate the Payable Total in F8 in the line below. *[2 marks]*

*(answer line: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The algorithm has two steps: (1) total price = Unit Price x Quantity, (2) Payable Total = total price - 5% Discount, where the discount has already been calculated in column C (question 4). In row 8:

```
F8: =D8*E8-C8
```

The formula is then copied down the whole column. A formula that recomputes the discount, `=D8*E8-0.05*D8*E8` or `=D8*E8*(1-5%)`, gives the same value and is also accepted, but the first form follows the algorithm exactly (it reuses the 5% Discount cell). Check with the example of question 4: 900 x 11 = 9,900; 9,900 - 495 = **9,405**.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the product Unit Price x Quantity, 1 mark for the subtraction of the discount.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calculate the total 5% Discount and total of the *Payable Total* in row 25.

Write down the formula in cell F25. *[1 mark]*

*(answer line: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The totals are obtained with the `SUM` function over the data rows of each column (header in row 1, data from row 2 to row 24, totals in row 25). The question asks for the cell **F25**, which lies under the Payable Total column:

```
F25: =SUM(F2:F24)
```

The total of the 5% Discount is calculated in the same way under its own column: `C25: =SUM(C2:C24)`. A selection of the two columns followed by the *AutoSum* button (Home > AutoSum, or Alt + =) writes both formulas at once. The data rows 2 to 24 are deduced from the borders of question 2 (range A1:G25 with the totals in row 25); if the data stopped before row 24 the range would be shortened accordingly.

*Marking:* 1 mark for `=SUM(F2:F24)` (or an equivalent range of the same column).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Set the font of row 25 to bold and size 14. *[1 mark]*

*Ensure that you have written down the formulae in the cells in questions 4, 5 and 6 above before attempting the questions that follow.*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click the heading of row **25** to select the whole row, then on the **Home** tab press **Bold** (Ctrl + B) and set the font size box to **14**.

*Marking:* 1 mark if row 25 is both bold and in size 14. (The reminder printed under the question asks the candidate to copy the formulae of questions 4 to 6 into the booklet before the columns are rearranged and the formulae move.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Rearrange the fields (columns) in this sheet to occur in the order SN, Name, Item, Unit Price, Quantity, 5% Discount and Payable Total. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The columns are in the order SN (A), Name (B), 5% Discount (C), Unit Price (D), Quantity (E), Payable Total (F), Item (G) (order deduced from the cell references of the paper). The requested order is SN, Name, **Item**, Unit Price, Quantity, **5% Discount**, Payable Total. Two moves are enough, using *Cut* and *Insert Cut Cells* (not Copy, so that the formulae keep working and their references are updated):

1. Select column **G** (Item), Cut (Ctrl + X), right-click the heading of column **C** and choose **Insert Cut Cells**: the order becomes SN, Name, Item, 5% Discount, Unit Price, Quantity, Payable Total.
2. Select column **D** (5% Discount), Cut, right-click the heading of column **G** (Payable Total) and choose **Insert Cut Cells**: the order becomes SN, Name, Item, Unit Price, Quantity, **5% Discount**, Payable Total.

Final layout: A SN, B Name, C Item, D Unit Price, E Quantity, F 5% Discount, G Payable Total. The formulae follow their cells: the discount is now `=0.05*D2*E2` in F2, the payable total `=D2*E2-F2` in G2, and the totals of row 25 become `=SUM(F2:F24)` in F25 and `=SUM(G2:G24)` in G25. (Dragging a column with the Shift key held down gives the same result.)

*Marking:* 1 mark for the Item column placed third, 1 mark for the remaining columns in the requested order.

questions.enonce_markdown: Format the numbers in the range D2:G25 to thousand separator without decimal place. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the rearrangement of question 8, the range **D2:G25** holds Unit Price (D), Quantity (E), 5% Discount (F) and Payable Total (G). Select the range, open **Format Cells** (Ctrl + 1) > **Number** tab > category *Number*, set *Decimal places* to **0** and tick **Use 1000 Separator (,)**. (The *Comma Style* button followed by two clicks on *Decrease Decimal* gives the same display.) The values 9,900 or 9,405 are then displayed with their separator and without decimals; the stored values are unchanged.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the thousand separator with 0 decimal places on the whole range.

questions.enonce_markdown: Insert a fill color of light blue to the cells that contain the totals in row 25. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
After the rearrangement, the totals of row 25 are in **F25** (total 5% Discount) and **G25** (total Payable Total). Select F25:G25 and, on the **Home** tab, open the *Fill Color* menu and choose a light blue (for example *Light Blue* in the standard colours, or *Blue, Accent 1, Lighter 60%*).

*Marking:* 1 mark for a light-blue fill on the cells that contain the totals only.

questions.enonce_markdown: Sort in ascending order, the table in **OldSales** by items. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click inside the table of the **OldSales** sheet (or select the whole table, headers included), then **Data > Sort**, tick *My data has headers*, choose the **Items** column in *Sort by* and the order **A to Z** (ascending). The whole table must be sorted, not only the Items column, so that every row keeps its own unit price and quantity. The items then appear in alphabetical order (for the eight items of the price list: Bulb, Cable, Cutlass, Floor rag, Gallon, Hand saw, Padlock, Spanner); if OldSales repeats an item on several rows, those rows are grouped together. The sort comes BEFORE the links of questions 12 and 13, because a link points to a cell address, not to an item.

*Marking:* 1 mark for the table sorted by Items, ascending, with the rows intact.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In C2 of the Summary sheet, type a formula to link C2 to a cell in OldSales that contains the unit price of spinners. Do similarly for the cells in the range C3:C9. *[1 mark]*

Write down the formula in cell C4 in the line below.

*(answer line: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A link is a formula made of an equals sign followed by a reference to a cell of another sheet: `=SheetName!CellAddress`. The cell of the Summary sheet is linked to the cell of the sorted OldSales table that contains the unit price of the item. The OldSales sheet is not printed, so its layout is assumed here: Item in column A, Unit Price in column B, Quantity in column C, the first item on row 2. The simplest way to write the link is to type `=` in the Summary cell, click the sheet tab OldSales, click the cell holding the price, and press Enter. For example, if after the sort of question 11 the unit price of spinners (spanners) is in cell B9 of OldSales:

```
C2: =OldSales!B9
```

The cell asked, **C4**, is linked in the same way to the unit price of the item listed on row 4 of the Summary sheet, for example `C4: =OldSales!B7` if that item is on row 7 of the sorted OldSales table (the exact address depends on the position of that item). Because the link is a plain reference, the Summary cell shows the price held in OldSales and follows any change made there. A lookup formula such as `=VLOOKUP(B4,OldSales!$A$2:$B$30,2,FALSE)` is an alternative that does not depend on the row position, but the question asks for a direct link to a cell.

*Marking:* 1 mark for a formula of the form `=OldSales!<cell>` pointing to a unit price (and the others filled in the same way in C3:C9).

questions.enonce_markdown:
In the Summary sheet, type a formula in D2 that will add the total quantity of spinners sold. Do similarly for the cells in the range D3:D9. Write down the formula in cell D2 in the line below. *[3 marks]*

*(answer line: write the formula in the line provided)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The quantity sold of an item is the sum of the Quantity values of all the OldSales rows whose Item is that item: this is a conditional sum, `SUMIF(range, criteria, sum_range)`. With the layout assumed in question 12 (OldSales: Item in A, Unit Price in B, Quantity in C, data from row 2 to row 30) and the name of the item written in cell B2 of the Summary sheet:

```
D2: =SUMIF(OldSales!$A$2:$A$30,B2,OldSales!$C$2:$C$30)
```

The ranges are absolute (`$A$2:$A$30`, `$C$2:$C$30`) so that they stay fixed when the formula is copied down to D3:D9, while the criterion `B2` is relative and becomes B3, B4, ... B9, giving one total per item. The version with the name typed inside the formula, `=SUMIF(OldSales!$A$2:$A$30,"Spanner",OldSales!$C$2:$C$30)`, gives the total for spanners too but would have to be edited for every row. For instance, if OldSales held three spanner rows of 20, 15 and 10 units, D2 would show 45.

*Marking:* 1 mark for `SUMIF` (or `SUMPRODUCT`), 1 mark for the correct range of items and criterion, 1 mark for the correct sum range, with the ranges anchored so that the formula can be copied down. The three sheets (Sales, OldSales and Summary) are then printed (File > Print > *Print Entire Workbook*, or each sheet in turn).
